fields.description:
## Context

Five tests across four modules exercise **surviving** features — attested/local
gate-source threading, snapshot materialization, fail-closed ref resolution, and
the `review_result` JSON-Schema contract — but reach them through
`rebar.llm.operations._review_ticket_impl`, the single-pass review engine ADR
0075 retired. Measured on `origin/main` at
`e2ed08b343a2be462de4433a93edbb5cbc062a52`, the engine is merely the *vehicle*:
none of the five asserts anything about reviewing a ticket.

That coupling blocks deleting the engine. Doing both at once would mix a removal
with five behaviour-preserving rewrites, and the rewrites carry the risk: a
careless one silently drops coverage of attested-mode gate reads, which exists
because of a real wrong-branch false-negative
(`test_gate_source_threading.py:1-8`). So this slice repoints the five tests
onto a surviving op **while the engine is still present**, changing no
production code. The engine's deletion then becomes a pure removal.

**The replacement op is verified, not assumed.** `rebar.llm.spec_scan.scan_epics_for_spec`
threads gate-source through the identical four-call shape as the engine —
`resolve_gate_handle` (`spec_scan.py:67` vs `operations.py:157`), `gate_read_root`
(`:69` vs `:158`), `apply_handle` (`:72` vs `:159`), `annotate_result` (`:73` vs
`:218`) — and takes the same `ref`, `source`, `repo_root`, `runner` arguments
(`spec_scan.py:44-55`). `annotate_result` stamps exactly
`PROVENANCE_KEYS = ("source", "verified_at_sha", "signable")`
(`gate_source.py:62`), the three keys these tests assert.

This was confirmed by running it, not by reading it: a scratch copy of
`test_attested_reads_pinned_ref_regardless_of_checkout_branch` rewritten onto
`scan_epics_for_spec`, asserting all five of its properties, passed alongside
the unmodified original (`2 passed`). That scratch test was then reverted.

## Approach

Rewrite each of the five call sites to `scan_epics_for_spec`, preserving every
existing assertion. It scans **epics**, so each test's fixture ticket changes
type from `task` to `epic` and the id is passed as `epics=[eid]`. No assertion
is weakened, removed, or retargeted; only the op beneath them changes. The diff
is tests-only.

## Scope

In scope, tests only: `tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_source_threading.py`,
`tests/interfaces/store/test_snapshot_environments.py`,
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py`,
`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_ops_characterization.py`.

Out of scope, verified rather than assumed:

- `src/rebar/llm/operations.py`, `src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py` — the engine
  stays live through this slice; deleting it is the **next** slice's job. AC5
  asserts it is still present.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py` — its
  `test_review_ticket_request_carries_model_max` (`def :414`, engine call `:428`)
  canNOT be repointed here: `spec_scan.py` does **not** call `max_output_cfg`
  (the call sites are `completion.py:405`, `plan_review/passes.py:157`,
  `operations.py:207`, `code_review/workflow_ops.py:650` — no `spec_scan`), so
  repointing it would assert a budget behaviour the replacement op does not have.
  It is deleted with the engine in the next slice.
- `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` (registry rows that are *removed*,
  not repointed), `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_budget.py`, and
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_review_as_workflow.py` — engine-specific
  behaviour with no surviving counterpart. Next slice.

## Testing

No new tests. Five existing tests are rewritten in place and must still pass with
their assertions unchanged. Locate each by name, not by line range.

**`tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_source_threading.py`** — three tests, all
reached through the shared helper `_ticket` (`def :87`, body `:88`), whose only
callers are these three (`:96`, `:121`, `:147`). Change that helper to create an
**epic** (and rename it to `_epic` to match), then:

- `test_attested_reads_pinned_ref_regardless_of_checkout_branch` — `def :94`,
  engine call `:101`. Keeps asserting `result["source"] == "attested"`,
  `verified_at_sha == main_sha`, `signable is True`,
  `Path(runner.captured_repo_path) != repo`, `captured_sentinel == "from-main\n"`.
- `test_attested_verdict_identical_across_checkout_branches` — `def :119`,
  engine call `:125` inside its local `run()` closure. Keeps asserting
  `on_other == on_main == "from-main\n"` across a branch switch.
- `test_local_mode_reads_checkout_and_is_unsigned` — `def :145`, engine call
  `:149`. Keeps asserting `source == "local"`, `signable is False`,
  `verified_at_sha is None`, read-root `== repo`, sentinel `"from-other\n"`.

The other tests in this module never touch the engine — `grep -n 'rebar\.llm\.'`
returns only `:20`, `:101`, `:125`, `:149`, `:196`, `:197` — so they are untouched.

**`tests/interfaces/store/test_snapshot_environments.py`** —
`test_attested_gate_against_non_rebar_sample_repo`, `def :107`, fixture ticket
created at `:130`, engine call `:135`. Keeps asserting `verified_at_sha ==
main_sha`, `signable is True`, that the read-root is a snapshot and not the
checkout, that `package.json` and `src/app.py` byte-match the sample project, and
that the snapshot contains no `src/rebar`. Its siblings (`:78`, `:87`) do not use
the engine.

**`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py`** —
`test_unresolvable_ref_attested_fails_closed`, `def :209`, fixture ticket at
`:211`, engine call `:215` inside `pytest.raises(SnapshotRefError)`. Keeps
asserting the same raise for `ref="no-such-ref-xyz"` in attested mode.

**`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_ops_characterization.py`** —
`test_review_result_validates_against_schema`, `def :68`, fixture ticket at
`:72`, engine call `:73`. Keeps validating the payload against
`schemas.REVIEW_RESULT`. This does **not** become redundant with
`test_scan_epics_for_spec_contract` (`def :60`), which already calls
`scan_epics_for_spec`: that test asserts only `_REQUIRED_KEYS <= set(result)` and
that `findings` is a list, whereas this one runs the full JSON-Schema validator.
Two of this module's five tests (`:23` `test_review_ticket_contract`, `:40`
`test_review_ticket_graph_target_kind`) are engine-behaviour tests with no
surviving counterpart; they are **not** touched here and are deleted in the next
slice.

## Acceptance criteria

Each criterion is a single command whose stated result is the pass condition.

- [x] **AC1 — three modules shed the engine entirely.**
      `git grep -n '_review_ticket_impl' -- tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_source_threading.py tests/interfaces/store/test_snapshot_environments.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py`
      prints nothing and exits 1.
- [x] **AC2 — the fourth sheds exactly its one repointed call.**
      `git grep -c '_review_ticket_impl' -- tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_ops_characterization.py`
      prints `2`, down from `3`. The two remaining are the engine-behaviour tests
      `def :23` and `def :40`, which the next slice deletes — this slice must not.
- [x] **AC3 — they call the replacement instead.**
      `git grep -ln 'scan_epics_for_spec' -- tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_source_threading.py tests/interfaces/store/test_snapshot_environments.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py`
      prints all three paths.
- [x] **AC4 — no production file changed.**
      `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- src docs` prints nothing. (Three
      dots, so `origin/main` advancing underneath does not register as this
      slice's change.)
- [x] **AC5 — the engine is still present.**
      `git grep -c 'def _review_ticket_impl' -- src/rebar/llm/operations.py`
      prints `1`.
- [x] **AC6 — the five tests still pass.** `pytest` over the four modules named in
      Scope exits 0, with no test skipped or deselected that ran before.
- [x] **AC7 — the suite is green.** `make verify` exits 0.
